what_it_does: Large language models (very large AI text systems) have been trained specifically on chip-design knowledge — for example, learning the specialized language of hardware description, timing constraints, and circuit analysis. However, these chip-specialist models are poor at following plain instructions from a human engineer, which makes them frustrating to use as assistants. ChipAlign addresses this by merging two separately trained models — one good at following instructions, one good at chip knowledge — without doing any extra training. The merging is done by blending the numerical weights (the millions of learned numbers that define a model's behavior) of the two models along a smooth mathematical path in 'weight space', a technique the authors call geodesic interpolation. The result is a single model that inherits both skills, though exactly how well this works in practice requires reading the full paper.
